scenes.title: The 30-lever shock generator: 'Please continue'
scenes.era: August 1961 - May 1962, Yale University interaction laboratory (Linsly-Chittenden Hall basement), New Haven, Connecticut

layout.description: Fluorescent-lit 1961 Yale basement laboratory divided by a solid partition wall with vertical striped drapes along the back wall. In the main room, the volunteer Teacher sits at a wooden desk facing the rectangular brushed-steel Type ZLB shock generator box (30 horizontal metal toggle levers from 15V on the left to 450V XXX on the right, circular voltmeter dial, red pilot lamps, and a four-quadrant 1-2-3-4 answer box on top). Beside and slightly behind him stands the stern Experimenter in a knee-length grey lab technician coat holding a clipboard. On the other side of the partition wall sits the Learner strapped into an armchair with an electrode on his wrist.

positions.who: Teacher (volunteer mannequin in 1960s white dress shirt with rolled-up sleeves)
positions.where: seated center at the wooden laboratory desk directly in front of the 30-lever shock generator panel
positions.facing: the brushed-steel switch console, turning his head back toward the Experimenter when hesitating

positions.who: Experimenter (31-year-old biology teacher role, mannequin in grey lab technician coat and dark tie)
positions.where: standing camera-right beside and slightly behind the Teacher's desk with a metal clipboard and stopwatch
positions.facing: down toward the Teacher and the switch panel

positions.who: Learner (47-year-old accountant role, mannequin in white shirt and vest)
positions.where: seated in the adjacent room behind the dividing partition wall, forearms strapped to the chair armrests
positions.facing: the partition wall separating him from the Teacher

props.name: 30-toggle voltage generator box (Type ZLB)
props.period_detail: wide brushed-steel and dark-grey rectangular console with 30 metal lever switches in a horizontal row labeled 15V to 450V in 15-volt steps, group plates from Slight Shock to Danger: Severe Shock and XXX, circular voltmeter gauge, and red/blue indicator bulbs
props.physical_behavior: metal toggle lever snaps down under the finger, bright red indicator light flashes on, blue energizer lamp flickers, voltmeter needle jumps to the right, internal relays click and buzz

props.name: four-quadrant answer box
props.period_detail: dark rectangular box mounted above the generator with translucent numbered windows 1, 2, 3, 4
props.physical_behavior: numbered quadrant lights up when the learner presses a response key, then stays dark after 315 volts

props.name: clipboard and pencil
props.period_detail: 1960s metal-clip laboratory board held by the Experimenter
props.physical_behavior: Experimenter taps the clipboard edge with a pencil as he delivers each standardized prod

props.name: wrist electrode and leather chair straps
props.period_detail: brown leather straps bucked across the Learner's forearms with a metal disc electrode wired to the wall
props.physical_behavior: leather straps pull taut when the Learner strains against the chair

actions.verb_sequence: reaches a trembling hand over the row of 30 metal levers -> presses a toggle switch down -> red indicator light flashes and voltmeter needle swings right -> jerks his hand back and turns toward the Experimenter
steps closer behind the Teacher's shoulder -> taps the clipboard -> gestures firmly toward the next switch along the 15V-to-450V panel

reactions.reaction: shoulders hunch forward, one hand clutches his own forehead and rubs his brow while his other hand hovers over the 450-volt XXX switches
stands rigid and impassive with arms angled over the clipboard, leaning slightly forward to issue the calm verbal prod

scenes.wardrobe: Teacher: 1960s white button-down dress shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbows, loosened dark tie, dark trousers. Experimenter: knee-length grey laboratory technician coat over white shirt and narrow black tie. Learner: 1960s dress shirt and suit trousers with jacket removed.
scenes.lighting: Bright, clean clinical daylight illumination filling the 1961 basement laboratory, catching the brushed-steel switch panel, red pilot lights, and matte-white porcelain figures.
scenes.recognition_hook: A man in a 1960s dress shirt sitting in front of the 30-lever 15V-to-450V XXX shock generator box while a man in a grey lab coat stands behind him saying 'Please continue' — the unmistakable image of the Milgram experiment.

key_visual.description: the teacher mannequin presses a lever on the thirty-switch shock generator while the grey-coated experimenter stands behind him saying please continue

scenes.title: Learner pounding on the dividing wall at 150V and 300V, then silence

layout.description: Split cross-section view bisecting the dividing partition wall between the two basement rooms. On the left side of the wall, the Learner sits strapped into the wooden armchair, hammering his fist against the partition wall at 300 and 315 volts before slumping completely still. On the right side of the wall, the Teacher sits at the 30-lever generator desk, flinching as the wall vibrates.

positions.where: left compartment, strapped into the armchair beside the dividing wall
positions.facing: the partition wall

positions.where: right compartment, seated at the 30-lever generator box beside the same wall
positions.facing: the generator panel and glancing sharply at the vibrating wall

positions.where: right compartment, standing behind the Teacher's chair
positions.facing: the Teacher

props.name: dividing partition wall
props.period_detail: solid wood-and-plaster laboratory partition separating Teacher and Learner
props.physical_behavior: shudders and vibrates as the Learner pounds his fist against it at 300 and 315 volts, knocking dust motes into the light

props.name: four-quadrant answer box and 30-lever panel
props.physical_behavior: red indicator light flashes and voltmeter needle swings right as the Teacher presses switches all the way to the 450V XXX lever while the answer box stays dark

actions.verb_sequence: pounds his clenched fist against the dividing wall twice -> strains against the leather wrist straps -> slumps motionless in the chair after 315 volts
jolts back from the desk as the wall thuds -> grips his hair with one hand -> reaches out and presses the final 450-volt XXX toggle switch down

reactions.reaction: trembles visibly, elbows braced on the wooden desk, burying his forehead in his palm before pushing the switch

scenes.wardrobe: Same 1961 Yale wardrobe: rolled-sleeve white dress shirt on Teacher, grey technician coat on Experimenter, dress shirt on strapped Learner.
scenes.lighting: Bright daylight across both sides of the bisected partition wall.
scenes.recognition_hook: Fists pounding through the laboratory wall followed by eerie silence while the volunteer still flips switches to 450 volts.

scenes.title: Touch-proximity variation: forcing the learner's hand onto the metal plate
scenes.era: 1961-1962, Yale University interaction laboratory (Milgram 1965 proximity and touch-proximity series)

layout.description: Single-room staging with the partition wall removed. The Learner sits at the same table right beside the Teacher, next to a flat wired metal plate connected to the 30-lever generator box. The grey-coated Experimenter stands beside them ordering the Teacher to press the Learner's hand down onto the plate.

positions.where: standing/leaning over the desk between the 30-lever generator and the Learner
positions.facing: the Learner and the metal contact plate

positions.where: seated immediately beside the Teacher at the same table
positions.facing: the metal contact plate, pulling his arm back

positions.where: standing camera-right with clipboard
positions.facing: the Teacher and Learner

props.name: flat metal contact plate
props.period_detail: brushed-steel rectangular contact plate wired to the voltage generator on the table
props.physical_behavior: slides slightly and sparks/buzzes as a hand is pressed down onto the metal surface while a red indicator light flashes

props.name: 30-lever voltage generator box
props.period_detail: same Type ZLB panel on the desk
props.physical_behavior: toggle switch snaps down and voltmeter needle swings right

actions.verb_sequence: yanks his hand off the metal contact plate -> twists his torso away from the desk
grabs the Learner's forearm with one hand -> forces the Learner's palm flat onto the metal plate -> recoils and pulls both hands back in refusal

reactions.reaction: steps backward away from the table, shaking his head and holding both palms up as obedience drops to 30 percent

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s rolled-sleeve dress shirt on Teacher, dress shirt on Learner, grey lab coat on Experimenter.
scenes.lighting: Bright studio daylight revealing the immediate physical closeness of Teacher and Learner.
scenes.recognition_hook: Having to physically hold the victim's hand down on the metal plate makes seven out of ten people refuse.

scenes.title: Defiance: refusing the bare order and dissenting peers walking out
scenes.era: 1961-1962, Yale University interaction laboratory (Prod 4 analysis and Experiment 17 two-peers defiance)

layout.description: At the 30-lever generator desk, the Teacher sits flanked by two peer teachers (or faces the Experimenter alone as Prod 4 'You have no other choice' is delivered). The peers push their chairs back and stand up to refuse, and the Teacher releases the switch lever and shoves his chair back from the console.

positions.where: center at the 30-lever generator desk, pushing his wooden chair back
positions.facing: turning squarely to face the Experimenter

positions.where: standing up beside the desk after pushing their chairs back
positions.facing: the Experimenter, arms folded or palms raised in refusal

positions.where: standing at right with clipboard extended
positions.facing: the refusing Teacher

props.name: 30-lever voltage generator box
props.physical_behavior: partial row of levers flips back up, voltmeter needle drops to zero, red indicator light clicks off

props.name: wooden laboratory chairs
props.physical_behavior: scrape and slide backward across the linoleum floor as the Teacher and peers stand up

actions.verb_sequence: steps forward -> points clipboard sharply at the switches ('You have no other choice, you must go on')
slam palms flat on the desk -> shove their wooden chairs backward -> stand up and step away from the switch console

reactions.reaction: stands tall with squared shoulders and raised palm, refusing to touch another switch
lowers the clipboard to his side as the session terminates

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s dress shirts and ties on Teacher and peers; grey technician coat on Experimenter.
scenes.lighting: Bright daylight illuminating the clear physical break from authority.
scenes.recognition_hook: When given a bare order ('you have no other choice') or when peers say no first, people push their chairs back and refuse.

scenes.title: The rigged draw and the real 45-volt sample shock on the teacher's wrist

layout.description: Before the test begins, the Experimenter holds two folded paper slips (both secretly reading 'Teacher') and then presses a metal wrist electrode with white paste onto the Teacher's own bare forearm at the generator console, flipping the third switch (45 volts) so the Teacher feels the only real electric jolt in the entire study.

positions.where: seated at the generator desk with right shirt sleeve rolled up, forearm resting near the third switch
positions.facing: his own wrist and the 45-volt switch

positions.where: leaning over the generator console beside the Teacher
positions.facing: the Teacher's wrist and the third toggle switch

props.name: two folded paper slips
props.period_detail: small white paper slips drawn from a hat, both inscribed 'Teacher'
props.physical_behavior: slip unfolds in the Teacher's hand while the Learner hides his slip

props.name: wrist electrode and 45-volt third switch
props.period_detail: metal contact strapped to the Teacher's wrist, wired to a hidden 45-volt battery on the third switch
props.physical_behavior: Experimenter flips the third toggle switch, a spark/red indicator light flashes, and the wire twitches

actions.verb_sequence: straps the metal electrode to the Teacher's wrist -> flips the third 45-volt lever switch down
jolts and yanks his forearm back from the console as the real 45-volt sample stings his wrist

reactions.reaction: rubs his stung wrist with his other hand, convinced the generator is genuinely live

scenes.wardrobe: Teacher in rolled-up white dress shirt; Experimenter in grey technician coat (matching M1 and M2 reference frames).
scenes.recognition_hook: The only person who ever felt a real electric jolt in Milgram's lab was the volunteer Teacher himself.

scenes.title: Same-room proximity variation: seeing the learner up close
scenes.era: 1961-1962, Yale University interaction laboratory (Milgram 1965 proximity condition)

layout.description: The Learner sits strapped in a chair just a few feet away from the Teacher inside the same room, visible in full view without a dividing wall. Seeing the Learner's body jolt in the same room drops obedience from 65 percent to 40 percent.

positions.where: seated at the 30-lever generator box
positions.facing: the Learner seated a few feet away in the same room

positions.where: seated in the armchair five feet in front of the desk in the same room
positions.facing: the Teacher

props.name: 30-lever voltage generator box
props.physical_behavior: red indicator light flashes once before the Teacher pulls his hand off the switch row

actions.verb_sequence: jerks against the chair straps right in front of the Teacher
flinches -> pulls his hand off the metal switch lever -> turns away from the console

reactions.reaction: drops both hands into his lap, unable to keep pressing switches while looking straight at the Learner

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s dress shirts and grey technician coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Put the victim in the same room and obedience drops from 65 percent to 40 percent.

scenes.title: Bridgeport commercial office variation: no Yale prestige
scenes.era: 1962, modest commercial office building in Bridgeport, Connecticut ('Research Associates of Bridgeport', Experiment 10)

layout.description: A plain, slightly worn downtown office room in Bridgeport with a frosted-glass door lettered 'Research Associates of Bridgeport', metal filing cabinets, and no Yale banners or ivy-covered walls. The same 30-lever generator sits on a plain office desk.

positions.where: seated at the plain office desk before the 30-lever generator
positions.facing: the switch panel

positions.where: standing beside a dented metal filing cabinet in the plain office
positions.facing: the Teacher

props.name: frosted-glass office door and metal filing cabinet
props.period_detail: 1960s commercial office door reading 'Research Associates of Bridgeport'
props.physical_behavior: door glass rattles slightly as the Teacher flips a switch and the red indicator light flashes

props.name: 30-lever voltage generator box
props.period_detail: same Type ZLB panel relocated to Bridgeport
props.physical_behavior: toggle switch clicks down, red light flashes, voltmeter needle swings right

actions.verb_sequence: glances around the plain commercial office -> hesitates -> still presses a metal toggle switch down as the red pilot light flashes

reactions.reaction: slumps his shoulders and wipes his brow with his sleeve as almost half (47.5 percent) still go to the end

scenes.lighting: Bright daylight through venetian blinds in a plain commercial office.
scenes.recognition_hook: Moving out of Yale into a plain Bridgeport office cut obedience, yet almost half still pressed every switch.

scenes.title: Burger 2009 replication stopping at the 150-volt turning point
scenes.era: 2009, Santa Clara University laboratory (Jerry M. Burger partial replication)

layout.description: Modern 2000s university psychology room with the recreated 30-lever generator box on a laminate desk. At the 150-volt tenth switch, the Learner shouts through the wall demanding to be let out; 70 percent of modern volunteers reach to press the next switch before the researcher steps in to stop the test.

positions.who: Modern Teacher (2009 volunteer mannequin in casual button-down shirt)
positions.where: seated at the desk in front of the 150-volt switch on the generator panel
positions.facing: the switch console

positions.where: standing beside the desk with a clipboard
positions.facing: the Teacher

props.name: 150-volt switch on the recreated generator panel
props.period_detail: tenth toggle lever marked 150 Volts (Strong Shock)
props.physical_behavior: Teacher presses the 150V switch, red light flashes, and his finger reaches onto the 165V lever before the Experimenter's hand covers the panel

actions.verb_sequence: presses the 150-volt toggle switch -> flinches as the wall vibrates -> reaches his finger forward to flip the next switch
steps in quickly -> places a palm over the switch row to halt the 2009 session at 150 volts

reactions.reaction: exhales and drops his hands onto the desk as the researcher stops the test

scenes.wardrobe: 2000s casual shirt on Teacher; lab coat on Experimenter.
scenes.recognition_hook: Repeated in 2009 up to the 150-volt turning point, 70 percent of people today still tried to keep going.

scenes.title: Fourteen Yale psychology seniors predict only 1 percent will obey
scenes.era: 1961, Yale University seminar classroom, New Haven

layout.description: A 1961 Yale seminar room with a chalkboard diagram of the 15V-to-450V switch panel. Fourteen senior psychology students sit at wooden desks writing their predictions on paper survey sheets, marking down 0 to 3 percent (mean 1.2 percent) near the bottom of the scale.

positions.who: Yale psychology seniors (mannequins in 1960s tweed jackets and sweaters)
positions.where: seated in rows at wooden seminar desks
positions.facing: the chalkboard diagram of the 30-lever generator

props.name: prediction survey sheets and fountain pens
props.period_detail: printed 0-to-100 percent scale sheets handed to 14 Yale seniors
props.physical_behavior: pen nib circles the 1 percent mark at the bottom of the page and slides the sheet across the desk

actions.verb_sequence: shakes his head dismissively at the 450-volt diagram -> scribbles a tiny mark at one percent on the paper sheet -> taps the pen down on the desk

reactions.reaction: lean back confidently in their wooden chairs, certain almost nobody would press the 450-volt switch

scenes.wardrobe: 1961 collegiate tweed jackets, cardigans, white shirts and ties.
scenes.recognition_hook: Yale psychology majors guessed only 1 in 100 people would go to 450 volts — fifty times lower than reality.

scenes.title: Stepping back when told 'it is for a good cause'

layout.description: Wide shot of the 1961 Yale basement laboratory where the Teacher pushes his chair back from the 30-lever generator box, stands up, and walks away from the grey-coated Experimenter while the red pilot light clicks off.

positions.where: standing beside the pushed-back chair in front of the 30-lever console
positions.facing: away from the switches, turning to face the Experimenter

positions.where: standing beside the desk with lowered clipboard
positions.facing: the Teacher

props.name: 30-lever generator box and wooden chair
props.period_detail: Type ZLB console with switches left unpressed
props.physical_behavior: wooden chair slides back across the floor and the red indicator light snaps dark

actions.verb_sequence: pulls his hand off the switch lever -> pushes the wooden chair backward -> stands up and steps away from the desk

reactions.reaction: stands upright with open palms, breaking the polite momentum of the room

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s rolled-sleeve dress shirt on Teacher, grey technician coat on Experimenter.
scenes.recognition_hook: Across all 30 variations, most people stopped — and knowing how the trap works lets you stop too.
